blockers.resolution: User must approve disabling, domestic fallback, or a compliant notice and consent policy before production cutover.

blockers.resolution: Record authoritative approvals and evidence during Stages 8 through 11.

blockers.reason: Docker Desktop cannot start com.docker.service from the current non-administrator session, so PostgreSQL and Redis integration verification is deferred.
blockers.resolution: Start Docker Desktop with administrator permission, then run rewrite:infra:up, rewrite:db:migrate, and rewrite:infra:check.

notes: Legacy remains the default runtime until Stage 12.
Rewrite uses a fresh database and does not migrate legacy SQLite or uploads.
The React home and minimal canvas receiver implementations are complete; authenticated end-to-end integration remains covered by the local Docker blocker.
The machine-readable work-package catalog is authoritative for scope, checks, acceptance, blockers, and successors.
Risk-tiered verification derives affected workspaces from staged paths; full repository check/build remains mandatory at stage and release gates and before a mid-stage push.
Rewrite-only visual polish is constrained by react-visual-delta-allowlist.json; Legacy remains read-only.
The concentrated React home and minimal canvas polish pass is complete with named Lucide imports, reduced-motion-safe micro interactions, responsive visual evidence, and no Legacy mutation.
The rewrite capability registry and /api/v1/capabilities expose credential-free readiness; production actions remain fail-closed unless a capability is verified.

Provider-neutral checkout now creates idempotent pending orders and payment attempts; only a signature-verified payment.succeeded webhook can mark an order paid, activate credits entitlement, and append a credit grant ledger entry. Production payment provider placeholders still fail closed with PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED until merchant integrations are verified.

WeChat Pay now has a Native checkout, query, refund, request-signing, callback-signature, and AES-GCM notification-decryption adapter with deterministic cryptographic fixtures. Configured production capability remains disabled until WECHATPAY_LIVE_VERIFIED is set only after merchant-environment evidence; live merchant verification remains deferred to Stage 11.

Alipay now has a precreate QR checkout, RSA2 form signing, asynchronous notification verification, query, and refund adapter with deterministic cryptographic fixtures. Configured production capability remains disabled until ALIPAY_LIVE_VERIFIED is set after merchant-environment evidence; live merchant verification remains deferred to Stage 11.
Identity provider contracts use deterministic development implementations and production fail-closed placeholders; real provider delivery, OAuth callbacks, and live verification remain deferred.
Moderation, notification, and audit records now have workspace-scoped PostgreSQL persistence, idempotency keys, retry timestamps, and worker recovery seams; real external providers remain deferred.

Billing domain foundation now defines integer-fen money, explicit order/payment/subscription state machines, and durable catalog/order/payment/subscription/entitlement/refund/invoice/event tables; merchant integrations remain deferred.

Payment provider contracts now fail closed in production and cover checkout, query, refund, renewal mandate, webhook signature verification, and provider-scoped replay protection; merchant credentials remain deferred.
Rewrite commercial routes now provide pricing, account, billing, credits, security, and data pages with existing account-menu entry points; unavailable services remain visibly fail-closed.
Compliance routes and the data-rights request foundation now cover legal notice, reporting, appeal, export, deletion, and closure seams; approvals and real processors remain release blockers.
Canvas document persistence now has a registered-node allowlist, explicit serializer, and snapshot migration registry; temporary and unknown nodes cannot be persisted as restored business nodes.
Canvas viewport math now provides deterministic pan, zoom-anchor, fit-bounds, and screen/world coordinate round trips without touching Legacy pointer behavior.
Canvas command history now provides bounded reversible document commands, project identity protection, and redo-branch invalidation without UI integration.
Canvas selection now supports single, additive, marquee, clear, and focus-safe reconciliation without UI integration.
Canvas transforms now provide pointer-delta movement and minimum-safe resize for selected nodes without UI integration or decorative path animation.
The rewrite Canvas adapter now renders engine nodes with granular selection and pointerup command commits; high-frequency pointermove avoids full React tree updates and Legacy remains untouched.
Canvas Stage 4 now has a 500-node selection/transform benchmark and rewrite Playwright gate; the next package starts Stage 5 tool-rail migration.
Rewrite Canvas tool rail now preserves tool identifiers, active/collapse state, submenu anchors, and mobile touch targets; shape and pen geometry remain in dedicated successor packages.
Rewrite Canvas now has a registered shape/arrow engine, deterministic pointer-derived arrow geometry, and complete shape submenu IDs.
Rewrite Canvas now has a registered text node with validated content and font formatting fields; Legacy text behavior remains untouched.
Rewrite Canvas pen now records actual pointer samples, commits a validated stroke on pointerup, and renders the same sampled SVG path.
Rewrite Canvas laser and eraser now use the canvas-relative pointer coordinates for transient trails and circular node hit testing; the laser tail expires after 420 milliseconds.
Rewrite Canvas shape and text format toolbars now appear only for a selected compatible node and update persistent node style fields without Legacy mutation.
Rewrite Canvas image nodes now expose the legacy action set through a typed toolbar command boundary; crop, upscale, expansion, and 3D execution remain in their dedicated successor packages.
Rewrite image transformation jobs now persist a typed source-node reference, dispatch through the Worker provider seam, and replace only the source image on completion.
Rewrite Canvas model nodes now restore as persistent business nodes and load Three.js plus GLTFLoader only when a visible model preview mounts.
Canvas Stage 5 now includes focus-safe keyboard commands, internal clipboard duplication, deletion, edge alignment, stacking, and front/back ordering through framework-independent engine commands.
Stage 3.5 builds fail-closed SaaS provider, commercial, and compliance foundations before full canvas migration.
The legacy runtime remains the default and is unchanged.

Video generation now reuses the existing APIMART task model through the rewrite Worker, persists a protected video result, and restores it as a typed Canvas video node; live provider verification remains deferred.
The rewrite 3D viewer now preserves lazy Three.js loading, OrbitControls interaction, ResizeObserver sizing, double-click reset, and visible fallback/failure states without changing Legacy.
Rewrite task logs now list workspace-scoped jobs with filters, pagination, refresh, detail, output navigation, and durable Worker recovery; Stage 6 now reaches its validation gate.

Rewrite projects now expose workspace-scoped full listing and durable create, read, versioned update, and delete API operations; project-library UI migration remains in its dedicated successor work packages.
Project snapshot reads and writes now use an explicit Canvas migration registry, normalize to registered persistent nodes, and fail closed for unsupported nonempty snapshots.
Protected media now resolves only through workspace-scoped upload IDs, provides inline and attachment responses with stable filenames, and never generates local storage-key URLs.
